text.p: - Slovenia's inflation rate should remain steady at around nine percent next year and economic growth should accelerate to four percent from a projected 3.5 percent this year, the state-sponsored Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said.

- President Milan Kucan will hold a second round of talks with representatives of parliamentary parties to break a deadlock over forming a new government. Kucan has to nominate his candidate for prime minister by January 3, 1997.
- Slovenian Health Insurance Company ZZZS will invest 1.3 billion tolars ($9.3 million) to introduce chip cards to replace outdated voucher booklets.
- Democratic Pensioners' Party of Slovenia, which has five seats in the 90-seat parliament, said it will support Janez Drnovsek as candidate for the new prime minister.
- President Milan Kucan said parliamentary representatives of minorities living in Slovenia had been under pressure recently from other parties to support one their candidates for prime minister.
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija beat Croatia Osiguranje from Split (Croatia) in Wednesday's basketball EuroLeague group C match 81:53.
- Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun attended NATO's ministerial meeting in Brussels on Wednesday, also met with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
